title: Validate determinism of the ported CCmpPosition (replay, state hash, save/load)
description:
WHY: determinism is the hard constraint on this epic and CCmpPosition is exactly the component the lockstep machinery watches most closely - ComputeStateHash in quick mode (run every turn) serializes only CID_Position. If the port perturbs position state at all, every networked game and every replay breaks. This is the gate that decides whether milestone 1 is actually done.

WHAT:
- Capture a baseline before/on the pre-port commit: run an existing replay with -replay and record per-turn state hashes plus DumpDebugState output. Then run the identical replay on the ported build and diff. Hashes must match on every turn, not just at the end.
- Save/load round-trip: serialize a mid-game state, deserialize it, confirm the resulting state hash equals the pre-save hash, and confirm resuming from the load stays in sync with the un-saved run.
- Two-client headless lockstep sanity run (see the headless multiplayer autostart flags) to confirm no out-of-sync is reported.
- If a mismatch appears, bisect it with DumpDebugState field-level diffing before changing anything, and record the root cause on this issue - a mismatch here is a design bug in the coexistence layer, not a CCmpPosition detail.
acceptance_criteria: An existing replay produces bit-identical per-turn state hashes before and after the port; a save/load round-trip preserves the state hash; a two-client headless match completes with no out-of-sync report. Evidence (commands run, hashes/diffs) recorded on this issue.

title: Windows build: vendored header-only source libs (entt) are not wired into libraries/win64 include path
description:
WHY: discovered while validating bd_0ad-1u1.1.3. Building on Windows currently requires a MANUAL, non-reproducible header copy, so a clean checkout cannot build.

ROOT CAUSE: extern_libs5.lua:21-29 sets libraries_source_dir conditionally - on Windows it is rootdir/libraries/win64/ (or win32), and only on non-Windows is it rootdir/libraries/source/. The helper add_source_include_paths(lib) (extern_libs5.lua:44-46) therefore resolves to libraries/win64/<lib>/include on Windows. But entt is vendored as a git submodule under libraries/source/entt/, and libraries/source/entt/build.sh copies its headers to libraries/source/entt/include/entt/ - a path the Windows build never looks at. entt is registered with add_source_include_paths('entt') at extern_libs5.lua:326.

Net effect: on Windows, libraries/win64/entt/include/entt/ must exist, and nothing in the repo creates it. get-windows-libs.bat fetches the SVN windows-libs bundle, which does not contain entt (entt was vendored into this repo separately). A clean Windows checkout + get-windows-libs.bat + premake + build FAILS to find entt headers until someone hand-copies them. That copy is what unblocked the build during bd_0ad-1u1.1.3 validation.

DO NOT FIX by rewriting add_source_include_paths/add_source_lib_paths to hardcode libraries/source/. That was attempted during validation and reverted: those two helpers are shared by benchmark, cpp-httplib, entt, fcollada, nvtt and spidermonkey, and on Windows fcollada/nvtt/spidermonkey come from the prebuilt win64 SVN bundle. Redirecting them all to libraries/source/ breaks the full pyrogenesis link on Windows even though the narrower 'test' target still builds.

LIKELY CORRECT FIXES (pick one, deliberately):
- give entt (and any future header-only source-vendored lib) its own extern_libs5.lua entry that points at libraries/source/<lib>/include on ALL platforms, since a header-only lib has no per-platform binaries; or
- have the Windows bootstrap copy header-only vendored libs into libraries/win64/<lib>/include as an explicit, scripted step; or
- introduce a distinct helper (e.g. add_header_only_source_include_paths) used only by header-only vendored libs.

Note the prior commit 4c7886e9aa claimed a green Windows build with entt, so verify whether that machine also had a hand-populated win64/entt or whether something else changed.
acceptance_criteria: A clean Windows checkout can build the test and pyrogenesis targets after only the documented bootstrap steps (get-windows-libs.bat, build-source-libs, premake, msbuild), with no manual header copying. fcollada/nvtt/spidermonkey still resolve to the prebuilt win64 bundle. Verified by inspecting the generated include paths for entt and for at least one prebuilt lib.
close_reason: Windows entt include path fixed via new add_header_only_source_include_paths helper; Debug/Release builds, 486-test suite, perf-guru review, and 60s two-client headless match (22,652 synced messages, no desync, matches main-branch behavior) all passed.

title: Benchmark EnTT storage access: member vs registry::get vs cached pool, and 1/2/3-pool split
description:
WHY: bd_0ad-1u1.1.3 mandates a three-way storage struct split (<Name>Template / <Name>State / <Name>Derived) in ADR-001 Appendix A, and EnTTComponent<>::Get<T>() caches storage-pool pointers to avoid entt registry::get<T>()'s per-access dense_map type-hash lookup. Both decisions were made from source analysis, not measurement. They are about to be baked into every ported component starting with CCmpPosition (bd_0ad-1u1.2.2), so settle them empirically first.

Source-derived expectations to confirm or refute:
- registry::get<T>(e) routes through assure<T>() -> pools.find(type_hash<T>::value()) on an entt::dense_map: ~4-5 serially dependent loads over 3 cache lines.
- cached-pool get is still ~5-6 dependent loads over 3-4 cache lines, because BOTH the sparse index (ENTT_SPARSE_PAGE=4096) and the payload (ENTT_PACKED_PAGE=1024) are paged. vs 1 usually-hot load for a plain member.
- Splitting into 3 pools may cost up to 3x the dependent-load chains and up to 12 cache lines instead of 4 on any path reading more than one struct, plus ~3x per-entity index overhead (~240KB vs ~80KB at 10k entities).

WHAT: use the existing Google Benchmark target (benchmarks project, binaries/system/benchmarks.exe, build/premake/premake5.lua ~line 1678). N=10k entities. Variants:
(a) virtual ICmp accessor reading a plain member (baseline)
(b) same accessor via registry.get<State>(e)
(c) same accessor via cached-pool pool->get(e)
(d) cached-pool touching 1 vs 2 vs 3 pools per call (settles the split convention)
(e) direct pool/view iteration over State for all entities (the eventual payoff case)

Axes that will otherwise make the result a lie: entity order creation-order AND shuffled; density 100% AND ~25% of entities carrying the component. Report ns/access, plus L1 miss counts if obtainable.

Predictions to check against: (a) ~2-4ns, (b) ~8-15ns, (c) ~5-9ns, (d) 3-pool ~2.5x the 1-pool number, (e) <1ns/entity. If (c) is not clearly better than (b), remove the pool caching from EnTTComponent and simplify. If (d) shows the 3-pool penalty dominating, merge <Name>Derived into <Name>State in ADR-001 Appendix A before CCmpPosition ports.
acceptance_criteria: Benchmark lands in the benchmarks target and runs. Results recorded on this bead. ADR-001 Appendix A's storage-split convention is either confirmed as-is or amended (Derived merged into State) based on the measurements, and EnTTComponent's pool caching is either confirmed or removed.

title: Port CCmpPosition to EnTT-backed storage behind the coexistence layer
description:
WHY: this is the milestone-1 deliverable. It proves the coexistence layer works on a real, hot, load-bearing native component without disturbing the ~hundreds of ICmpPosition call sites across simulation, rendering and AI code.

WHAT:
- Move CCmpPosition state into the entt storage structs from the audit task, accessed through the EnTT component helper. The class keeps deriving from ICmpPosition, keeps DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR-style per-entity allocation, and keeps its ClassInit subscriptions (MT_TurnStart, MT_TerrainChanged, MT_WaterChanged, MT_Deserialized) plus the existing dynamic MT_Interpolate subscription via DynamicSubscriptionNonsync.
- Serialize/Deserialize must emit and consume exactly the same fields in exactly the same order as today. The serialization version (IComponent::GetSerializationVersion) must not need bumping; if you believe it does, stop and escalate, because that means the format changed.
- No public ICmpPosition signature changes, so no caller changes. Any caller diff is a red flag that state semantics drifted.
- Preserve the special cases in the existing implementation: the turret parent/child relationships, the !m_InWorld "undefined junk" coordinates, and the interpolation state that must survive a Deserialize by being recomputed rather than loaded.
acceptance_criteria: Full build succeeds; binaries/system/test.exe passes; zero changes to files that merely call ICmpPosition; CCmpPosition no longer stores its state in class members.

title: Audit CCmpPosition state and define its EnTT storage structs
description:
WHY: CCmpPosition (source/simulation2/components/CCmpPosition.cpp) mixes three categories of state in one class, and the port must not accidentally serialize or fail to serialize any of them. This audit is a paper exercise that de-risks the actual port and produces the struct layout the rest of the feature builds on.

WHAT: enumerate every member and classify it:
- Template/static state set from the XML schema in Init: m_AnchorType, m_Floating, m_FloatDepth, m_RotYSpeed.
- Dynamic serialized state: m_InWorld, m_X/m_Z, m_LastX/m_LastZ, m_PrevX/m_PrevZ, m_Y, m_LastYDifference, m_RelativeToGround, m_ConstructionProgress, m_RotX/m_RotY/m_RotZ, m_TurretParent, m_TurretPosition, m_Turrets (std::set<entity_id_t>).
- Explicitly not serialized: m_ActorAnchorType, m_InterpolatedRotX/Y/Z, m_LastInterpolatedRotX/Z, m_ActorFloating, m_EnabledMessageInterpolate.
Then define the entt component structs, keeping the three categories separate per the coexistence-layer convention. Flag the awkward members explicitly: m_Turrets is a heap-allocating std::set inside what should be dense storage (decide whether it stays inline, moves to a side table, or is a separate sparse entt component present only on entities that actually have turrets), and note that the existing Serialize/Deserialize implementation and its exact field order must be reproduced unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Every CCmpPosition member is accounted for in exactly one category; the proposed struct layout is written down and reviewed; the decision on m_Turrets storage is recorded with rationale.

title: Add simulation-owned entt::registry with entity_id_t mapping and lifecycle hooks
description:
WHY: EnTT-backed components need a registry created, reset, and destroyed in lockstep with legacy simulation state, plus a mapping between the two entity identity schemes. Getting lifecycle wrong here shows up as stale registry rows surviving a ResetState or a deserialize, which is a silent desync.

WHAT (per the ADR from the design task):
- Introduce the registry owner (e.g. source/simulation2/system/EnTTWorld.h/.cpp) and expose it where components can reach it - most likely off CSimContext, since IComponent already holds a const CSimContext* and every component can call GetSimContext().
- Implement CreateEntity/DestroyEntity/Lookup for the entity mapping, handling SYSTEM_ENTITY (id 1) and local entities (ENTITY_IS_LOCAL) explicitly.
- Wire the lifecycle into CComponentManager: AllocateEntityHandle/AddComponent create the registry entity; DestroyComponentsSoon/FlushDestroyedComponents destroy it (destruction is deferred today precisely because the manager may be on the call stack, and registry destruction must respect the same deferral); ResetState clears registry and mapping; DeserializeState rebuilds them.
- No component uses it yet: this task is purely additive and must be a behavioural no-op.

ACCEPTANCE: binaries/system/test.exe passes unchanged; a fresh sim, a ResetState, and a save/load cycle each leave registry and mapping consistent (asserted in tests); no existing component modified.
design:
Implemented per ADR-001. CComponentManager (source/simulation2/system/ComponentManager.h/.cpp) now owns an entt::registry (held via std::unique_ptr<entt::registry> for pimpl - see below) plus a bidirectional entity_id_t<->entt::entity map: std::unordered_map<entity_id_t, entt::entity> m_EntityMap (forward) and a new SimEntityId{entity_id_t id} component attached to every registry entity (reverse). New private helpers CreateRegistryEntity/DestroyRegistryEntity are called from the existing choke points: AllocateEntityHandle (creates) and FlushDestroyedComponents (destroys, alongside the existing deferred-destruction queue). ResetState clears both. DeserializeState needed no new code: it already flows through ResetState + InitSystemEntity + AllocateEntityHandle (via LookupEntityHandle(ent, true) inside ConstructComponent call sites) so the registry/mapping rebuild for free. Public accessors added: entt::registry& GetRegistry()/const, entt::entity LookupRegistryEntity(entity_id_t) const. No gameplay component touches the registry; purely additive, verified behavioral no-op via full test suite (481 tests, was 478, pass unchanged plus 3 new).

registry.clear() verification: did NOT rely on empirical clear() behavior. Per the ADR's own escape hatch, ResetState replaces the registry object outright (m_Registry = std::make_unique<entt::registry>()) rather than calling clear(), sidestepping the question of whether entt 4.0's storage pools return to a fresh-equivalent state after clear() for our usage pattern. This is provably equivalent to a fresh registry by construction, so a determinism/state-hash risk from stale pool state was eliminated rather than merely tested for.

Header layout deviation from the ADR sketch (functionally identical, packaging only): GetRegistry() and the registry member could not be declared with the full entt::registry type inline in ComponentManager.h as originally sketched, because that header is transitively included by network/rlinterface/lobby/engine/graphics/atlas/gui static-lib projects that had no entt include path wired up - build broke with C1083 (cannot open entt/entity/registry.hpp) across ~7 projects. Fixed by: (1) ComponentManager.h now only includes the lightweight <entt/entity/fwd.hpp> (entt::entity is a complete enum there; entt::registry is forward-declared incomplete), (2) m_Registry is std::unique_ptr<entt::registry> instead of a by-value member (dtor/assignment already out-of-line in ComponentManager.cpp, which is the only TU that includes the full <entt/entity/registry.hpp>), (3) GetRegistry() declared in the header, defined in the .cpp. Also added "entt" to extern_libs for network/rlinterface/lobby/engine/graphics/atlas/gui in build/premake/premake5.lua (header-only, same pattern as tracy's existing entries) and regenerated build/workspaces/vs2022/*.vcxproj via premake5.

Tests added in source/simulation2/tests/test_ComponentManager.h (TestComponentManager is already a friend class): test_EnTT_freshSim, test_EnTT_resetState, test_EnTT_saveLoadCycle - assert SYSTEM_ENTITY/normal/local entities get a valid registry entity + correct SimEntityId on fresh construction, that ResetState fully clears the mapping and a subsequent InitSystemEntity reproduces the same first-registry-entity index as an untouched fresh manager, and that a SerializeState/DeserializeState round trip rebuilds the registry mapping for every saved entity. test_EnTT.h (the pre-existing placeholder smoke test) untouched.

Also committed source/simulation2/docs/ADR-001-EnTT-IComponent-Coexistence.md, which was present on disk (referenced by this task) but untracked/never committed by the prior design task (bd_0ad-1u1.1.1).
acceptance_criteria: binaries/system/test.exe passes unchanged; a fresh sim, a ResetState, and a save/load cycle each leave registry and mapping consistent (asserted in tests); no existing component modified.
close_reason: EnTT coexistence infrastructure implemented and validated: registry ownership, entity_id_t<->entt::entity mapping, lifecycle wiring into AllocateEntityHandle/FlushDestroyedComponents/ResetState, unit tests, full test suite green (481 tests).

title: Provide reusable EnTT-backed component helper (base/CRTP + allocator macro)
description:
WHY: without a shared helper, each ported component hand-rolls registry access and the ADR invariants (stable proxy address, no order-dependent iteration, storage struct separation) get re-violated per component. This is the API that makes the rest of the migration mechanical.

WHAT:
- Add a helper (e.g. EnTTComponent<Derived, StorageStructs...> in source/simulation2/system/) that a native component inherits alongside its ICmpXxx interface, giving it typed accessors to its registry rows for GetEntityId(), emplace-on-Init, erase-on-Deinit, emplace-on-Deserialize.
- Provide an allocator macro analogous to DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR (Component.h) if the existing one is insufficient. The proxy must still be individually heap-allocated with a stable address.
- Decide and document the storage split convention: template/static state, dynamic serialized state, and non-serialized derived/interpolation state belong in separate entt component structs, so later work can iterate hot data without dragging cold data through cache.
- Handle the mock-component path (AddMockComponent, DEFAULT_MOCK_COMPONENT in ComponentTest.h) so unit tests injecting mocks still work.

ACCEPTANCE: A throwaway test component built on the helper can be registered, Init-ed, serialized, deserialized and destroyed through normal CComponentManager paths in a unit test, with no CComponentManager call-site changes beyond the lifecycle hooks from the previous task.
acceptance_criteria: A throwaway test component built on the helper can be registered, Init-ed, serialized, deserialized and destroyed through normal CComponentManager paths in a unit test, with no CComponentManager call-site changes beyond the lifecycle hooks from the previous task.
close_reason:
Delivered EnTTComponent<Derived, TStorage...> CRTP mixin at source/simulation2/system/EnTTComponent.h, plus ADR-001 Appendix A documenting the storage-split convention, a worked-example registry-backed test component (CCmpTest1EnTT), and 5 unit tests.

Acceptance criterion met and empirically verified: CCmpTest1EnTT is registered (TypeList + REGISTER_COMPONENT_TYPE + AddComponent), Init-ed, serialized, deserialized (via ComponentTestHelper::Roundtrip, which builds a second CComponentManager and does ConstructComponent + Deserialize) and destroyed (DestroyComponentsSoon + FlushDestroyedComponents) through normal CComponentManager paths. ComponentManager.h/.cpp were NOT modified at all - verified by git diff - so the 'no call-site changes beyond bd_0ad-1u1.1.2's lifecycle hooks' constraint holds strictly.

Validation: Release x64 and Debug x64 both build with 0 errors / 0 warnings; test suite 486/486 OK in BOTH configs (481 baseline + 5 new). Debug matters independently because the mixin's Get<T>() correctness guards use the debug-only ASSERT macro, compiled out in Release. test_serialization (which hardcodes an MD5 embedding raw CIDs) passes: COMPONENT(Test1EnTT) was placed after COMPONENT(Test2Scripted) specifically to preserve CID_Test1A=1 and CID_Test2A=4, with a comment in TypeList.h recording the constraint.

Design decisions worth carrying forward:
- Mixin does NOT inherit IComponent (avoids duplicate/virtual base); reaches GetEntityId/GetSimContext via CRTP.
- Exposes no entt::registry accessor, and Get<T>() static_asserts T is one of the component's own declared storage structs - ADR Decision 5 enforced by construction, not convention.
- DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR needs NO analogue: plain 'new CCmpX()' already gives the address-stable, individually-heap-allocated proxy Decision 3 requires. Reasoning recorded in ADR Appendix A so it isn't re-litigated.
- Get<T>() caches storage-pool pointers rather than calling registry::get<T>(), which routes through assure<T>() -> pools.find(type_hash<T>) (a dense_map probe) on EVERY access. Independently perf-reviewed.
- No view/pool iteration introduced anywhere (ADR Decision 4) - verified by grep.

Honest caveat recorded in ADR Appendix A: even with pool caching this is an immediate per-access INCREASE (~5-6 dependent loads vs 1; both entt's sparse index and payload are paged), not neutral. The payoff needs real systems iterating pools directly.

Follow-ups filed: bd_0ad-1u1.1.6 (benchmark to settle the 3-way split + pool caching empirically; now blocks bd_0ad-1u1.2.2), bd_0ad-1u1.1.7 (guard the ResetState proxies-destroyed-before-registry-replaced invariant; deliberately not done here as it would breach the no-call-site-changes constraint), bd_0ad-1u1.3 (convert a hot CCmpPosition consumer to direct pool iteration so the milestone is judged on net perf), bd_0ad-ahy (QueryInterface/CmpPtr hash lookups in hot loops), bd_0ad-5je (P1 bug: Windows build needs a manual entt header copy into libraries/win64 - pre-existing, found during validation).

NOT committed - awaiting review.

title: Establish determinism guard rails for EnTT-backed components
description:
WHY: determinism is a hard constraint, and the most dangerous new failure mode EnTT introduces is iteration order. entt views and groups iterate in dense-storage order, which depends on insertion and swap-and-pop erase history - so it can differ between two clients that reached the same logical state by different paths, and between a live game and its replay. A desync from this is silent and extremely expensive to debug later.

WHAT:
- Write down the rules: (a) never mutate simulation state while iterating a view in storage order; ordered iteration must be driven by ascending entity_id_t, as the legacy std::map iteration does today; (b) serialized output must never depend on storage order; (c) no reinterpret_cast between entity_id_t and entt::entity.
- Add enforcement where cheap: debug-build assertions in the helper, and/or an ordered-iteration utility that sorts by entity_id_t so callers get a correct default instead of a footgun.
- Evaluate whether entt::registry::sort can keep storage in ascending-entity order, and record the cost/benefit. If adopted it must be applied deterministically: the same sort at the same points on every client.
- Document how a suspected EnTT-induced desync is diagnosed with existing tooling: per-turn ComputeStateHash, DumpDebugState diffing, and ReplayTurnManager.

ACCEPTANCE: Rules documented in-repo next to the helper, and at least one debug assertion or ordered-iteration utility exists that would catch order-dependent mutation during view iteration.
acceptance_criteria: Rules documented in-repo next to the helper, and at least one debug assertion or ordered-iteration utility exists that would catch order-dependent mutation during view iteration.
close_reason: Determinism rules documented (EnTT-Determinism-Rules.md) and enforcement utility (CPoolStructureGuard + ForEachOrderedByEntityId) added in EnTTOrderedIteration.h; perf-guru findings fixed by software-engineer; Debug+Release build clean; 486/486 tests pass; 60s headless 2-client match verified by devops.

title: Design and document the EnTT/IComponent coexistence pattern (ADR)
description:
WHY: every subsequent task depends on settled answers to a handful of questions that are cheap to decide on paper and expensive to discover mid-port. This must be written down because the migration will run over many components and many sessions.

WHAT: produce a short design record (in-repo doc under source/simulation2/, or the design field of this issue) answering, with reference to actual code:
1. Registry ownership: who owns the entt::registry (CSimContext vs CComponentManager vs a new CEnTTWorld), and how its lifetime interacts with CComponentManager::ResetState(), InitSystemEntity(), and DeserializeState().
2. Entity identity: how entity_id_t maps to entt::entity. entity_id_t is a u32 with a local-entity tag bit (ENTITY_TAGMASK, Entity.h) and is never reused; entt::entity is a recycled index+version. Decide between (a) a map in both directions, or (b) forcing entt entity values to equal entity_id_t via registry.create(hint) and never recycling. Record the memory and determinism consequences of each.
3. Proxy object model: the IComponent subclass stays one-instance-per-entity, because DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR does "new CCmpX()" and that raw address is cached in SEntityComponentCache (Entity.h) and in the m_ComponentsBy* maps. Confirm the proxy holds only a registry handle and forwards all state access to the registry, and that its address stays stable for the entity lifetime.
4. Serialization invariance: document that CComponentManager::SerializeState / ComputeStateHash / DumpDebugState iterate m_ComponentsByTypeId in (component type id, ascending entity_id) order and call IComponent::Serialize, so as long as proxy registration is unchanged the output stays byte-identical - and that EnTT view iteration order (swap-and-pop, unstable) must therefore never leak into serialized state or into any state-mutating logic.
5. Where the boundary sits for migrated components that must talk to not-yet-migrated ones (answer: they keep using CmpPtr/QueryInterface; no new coupling is introduced).

ACCEPTANCE: A written design record covers all five questions, with an actual decision (not a menu of options) recorded for registry ownership and entity mapping, reviewed by the user before implementation tasks start.
design: ADR at source/simulation2/docs/ADR-001-EnTT-IComponent-Coexistence.md. (1) Registry ownership: entt::registry is a private member of CComponentManager exposed via GetRegistry(); not CSimContext (which outlives the manager and is a non-owning view) and no new CEnTTWorld. Created with the manager; SYSTEM_ENTITY registry entity created in InitSystemEntity() right after AllocateEntityHandle; ResetState() tears the registry down AFTER the existing reverse-order Deinit/dealloc loop and must leave it observably identical to a fresh registry; DeserializeState keeps its existing reset+ConstructComponent+Deserialize shape, registry is never snapshotted as a blob so the save format is unchanged. Per-manager, never global (secondary manager/context pair exists). (2) Entity identity: bidirectional map - forward entity_id_t->entt::entity hash map on the manager, reverse via a SimEntityId{entity_id_t} component on every registry entity. create(hint) is REJECTED: default ENTT_ID_TYPE=uint32_t gives a 20-bit entity_mask 0xFFFFF so FIRST_LOCAL_ENTITY (1<<29) is unrepresentable and normal ids cap at ~1.05M; a 64-bit entity type would work but ENTT_SPARSE_PAGE=4096 means one local entity at index 2^29 forces a ~1MB page directory per storage pool per component type. Cost: one map entry + 4 bytes per live entity. Registry entity values are never serialized/hashed/ordered/exposed to JS and the map is never iterated for state-affecting work, so recycling stays invisible. Entries created in AllocateEntityHandle, destroyed in FlushDestroyedComponents. (3) Proxy model: confirmed unchanged - CCmpX stays a one-instance-per-entity IComponent from DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR (new CCmpX()), registered identically in m_ComponentsByInterface/m_ComponentsByTypeId/SEntityComponentCache; it keeps only a cached entt::registry* + entt::entity and forwards all state access; address is stable for the entity lifetime (honouring the 'unit motion manager relies on components not moving in memory' invariant at ComponentManager.cpp:793). No caller may hold references INTO registry storage across add/remove. AddMockComponent unaffected. (4) Serialization invariance: SerializeState/ComputeStateHash iterate m_ComponentsByTypeId as (ascending ComponentTypeId, ascending entity_id_t) and DumpDebugState inverts to (ascending entity_id_t, ascending ComponentTypeId); since proxy registration is untouched, output stays byte-identical - acceptance test per migration is identical ComputeStateHash + DumpDebugState on the same replay. EnTT swap-and-pop view order must never leak into serialization or into order-sensitive mutation (shared accumulation, first-match-wins, m_RNG consumption, message emission, entity creation/destruction); views allowed only for order-independent per-entity work or after sorting by entity_id_t. Enforced by bd_0ad-1u1.1.4. (5) Boundary: migrated components reach non-migrated ones only via CmpPtr/QueryInterface and messages, no new coupling; no direct cross-component registry access even between two migrated components; multi-component views are a later explicitly-scoped optimisation requiring their own determinism argument.
acceptance_criteria: A written design record covers all five questions, with an actual decision (not a menu of options) recorded for registry ownership and entity mapping, reviewed by the user before implementation tasks start.
close_reason: ADR approved by user; ResetState/registry.clear() equivalence to be verified empirically in bd_0ad-1u1.1.2

title: Port CCmpPosition to EnTT-backed storage (milestone 1)
description:
WHY: the coexistence layer is unproven until a real, load-bearing component runs on it. CCmpPosition is the right first target: it is CT_Native, it has no JS implementation, it is the single most performance-relevant per-entity component (every unit has one, and it is the only component ComputeStateHash inspects in "quick" mode - see the `quick && cit->first == CID_Position` check in ComponentManagerSerialization.cpp), and its state is plain fixed-point data plus a small set<entity_id_t> of turrets.

WHAT: move CCmpPosition state (source/simulation2/components/CCmpPosition.cpp) into entt registry component structs via the coexistence layer, keeping the class an ICmpPosition/IComponent subclass with unchanged public API, unchanged message subscriptions (MT_TurnStart, MT_TerrainChanged, MT_WaterChanged, MT_Deserialized, plus the dynamic MT_Interpolate subscription), and byte-identical Serialize/Deserialize.

ACCEPTANCE FOR THE FEATURE: existing replays reproduce identically, per-turn state hashes match pre-port, save/load round-trips, and no ICmpPosition caller needed to change.

OUT OF SCOPE: rewriting position logic, changing the fixed-point maths, touching CCmpUnitMotion or any other component.

title: EnTT coexistence layer for native IComponent types
description:
WHY: before any component can be migrated, there must be a reusable, determinism-safe mechanism for a native C++ component to keep its IComponent identity (so QueryInterface, CEntityHandle component caches, message subscriptions, and serialization all keep working) while its actual state lives in an entt::registry. Without this layer, each port would reinvent entity mapping and lifecycle handling, and each would be a fresh determinism risk.

WHAT: build the infrastructure only - no gameplay component is ported here.
- A single simulation-owned entt::registry with a defined lifetime tied to CSimContext / CComponentManager (created, reset by ResetState, torn down with the sim).
- A bidirectional entity_id_t <-> entt::entity mapping, since entity_id_t is a u32 with tag bits (ENTITY_TAGMASK for local entities, SYSTEM_ENTITY == 1) and is never reused, whereas entt::entity encodes a recycled index+version. These are NOT interchangeable and must not be reinterpret_cast into each other.
- A CRTP/base helper so a component class declares its storage struct(s) and gets registry-backed accessors, with the IComponent proxy object still allocated per entity by DEFAULT_COMPONENT_ALLOCATOR (its address is stored in SEntityComponentCache and must remain stable for the entity lifetime).
- Explicit determinism rules and guard rails.

OUT OF SCOPE: scripted components, removing anything from CComponentManager, changing serialization format.

title: Convert legacy ECS to EnTT
description:
Migrate 0ad simulation2 from the bespoke CComponentManager/IComponent ECS to EnTT (libraries/source/entt, header-only, already wired into premake via build/premake/extern_libs5.lua).

WHY: the legacy system stores each component as a heap-allocated IComponent* in std::map/unordered_map keyed by entity_id_t, which is pointer-chasing, cache-hostile, and offers no way to iterate component data contiguously. EnTT gives dense per-type storage and views, which is a precondition for later data-oriented simulation work.

SCOPE DECISIONS (settled, do not re-litigate):
1. INCREMENTAL COEXISTENCE, not a big-bang rewrite. EnTT and CComponentManager/IComponent coexist long-term. Components migrate one at a time; every migrated component keeps conforming to the IComponent interface (Init/Deinit/HandleMessage/Serialize/Deserialize) and to the existing message subscription system, so the rest of the engine is untouched.
2. JS-SCRIPTED COMPONENTS (CT_Script / CT_ScriptWrapper) ARE OUT OF SCOPE for milestone 1. Only native C++ (CT_Native) components are touched.
3. DETERMINISM IS A HARD CONSTRAINT FROM DAY ONE. 0ad has lockstep multiplayer (TurnManager/NetClientTurnManager, per-turn ComputeStateHash) and replay reproduction (ReplayTurnManager, commands.txt). Any EnTT-backed component must produce bit-identical serialization, state hashes, and simulation results. Nothing about determinism is deferred to "later".

MILESTONE 1 DELIVERABLE: one real, currently-native, non-scripted component (candidate: CCmpPosition) storing its data in an entt::registry while still presenting as an IComponent, plus the reusable coexistence layer that made it possible, plus determinism validation (replay + state hash + save/load).

KEY ARCHITECTURAL ANCHOR (verified in code): CComponentManager::SerializeState / ComputeStateHash / DumpDebugState iterate m_ComponentsByTypeId (std::map<ComponentTypeId, std::map<entity_id_t, IComponent*>>) and call IComponent::Serialize per entity in ascending entity_id order. If a migrated component keeps a per-entity IComponent proxy registered with the manager exactly as today, and only its *storage* moves into the registry, serialization order and bytes are preserved for free. EnTT storage order (swap-and-pop) must therefore never be observable by simulation logic.

title: Windows build: benchmark lib not wired into libraries/win64 (same bootstrap-reproducibility gap as entt)
description: WHY: discovered by principal-engineer while designing the fix for bd_0ad-5je (entt header-only include path bug). The 'benchmark' extern lib entry in build/premake/extern_libs5.lua uses add_source_include_paths/add_source_lib_paths, which on Windows resolve into libraries/win64/benchmark/. But libraries/win64/ is the SVN-managed prebuilt bundle fetched by get-windows-libs.bat, and (unlike fcollada/nvtt/spidermonkey) there is no benchmark directory in that bundle -- Google Benchmark is vendored as source (libraries/source/benchmark) like entt. Unlike entt, benchmark is a REAL compiled library (not header-only), so the fix is different from bd_0ad-5je's header-only-include-path fix: it likely needs an actual Windows build step/script that compiles libraries/source/benchmark and stages the .lib/.h output into libraries/win64/benchmark/, or an equivalent premake-side special case. NOT YET CONFIRMED whether a clean Windows checkout can currently build the 'benchmarks' target; needs verification (attempt premake + msbuild of the benchmarks project on a checkout without a hand-populated libraries/win64/benchmark/) before deciding the exact fix.
acceptance_criteria: Clean Windows checkout (get-windows-libs.bat + build-source-libs + premake + msbuild) can build the 'benchmarks' target with no manual file staging, OR this bead is closed as not-a-bug if investigation shows benchmark is already correctly bootstrapped on Windows via some other existing mechanism.

title: Reduce QueryInterface/CmpPtr hash-lookup cost in hot simulation loops
description:
WHY: surfaced during the perf review of the EnTT coexistence layer (bd_0ad-1u1.1.3), and orthogonal to the EnTT migration. For hot per-entity state access, obtaining the component proxy at all is a comparable or larger cost than the state indirection the EnTT work is optimising. CComponentManager::QueryInterface does an std::unordered_map lookup per call (m_ComponentsByInterface[iid].find(ent), ComponentManager.cpp), and CmpPtr wraps it. SEntityComponentCache already exists as the fast path when a CEntityHandle is in hand, but hot loops that only have an entity_id_t pay the hash lookup.

WHAT: profile the hot simulation loops, identify the ones resolving components by entity_id_t per iteration, and hoist to CEntityHandle/SEntityComponentCache or cache the proxy pointer across the loop (legal: proxy addresses are stable for the component lifetime - see ComponentManager.cpp:793 and ADR-001 Decision 3). Higher leverage than the EnTT accessor indirection and independent of it.
acceptance_criteria: Hot loops identified by profiling no longer perform a per-iteration interface hash lookup. Before/after numbers recorded. No behavioural or determinism change.

title: Convert one hot CCmpPosition consumer to direct pool iteration (net-perf validation for the EnTT milestone)
description:
WHY: as designed, the coexistence layer makes per-access cost WORSE, not better. Even with EnTTComponent's cached pool pointers, Get<T>() is ~5-6 serially dependent loads over 3-4 cache lines (both the sparse index at ENTT_SPARSE_PAGE=4096 and the payload at ENTT_PACKED_PAGE=1024 are paged) versus 1 usually-hot load for the member variable it replaces. Because each access already sits behind a virtual ICmpX call, the marginal cost is more like +30-60% per accessor call than 6x - but it is an increase. The payoff only arrives when a real system iterates a pool directly and the sparse lookup disappears entirely.

Consequence: porting CCmpPosition (bd_0ad-1u1.2.2) on its own lands a measurable regression with no offsetting win, and the milestone would have to be judged on faith rather than on numbers.

WHAT: after CCmpPosition is registry-backed, convert one genuinely hot consumer to direct pool iteration so the milestone can be evaluated on NET performance. Interpolation is the obvious candidate: it touches every entity every frame and is per-entity order-independent, so it is permitted under ADR-001 Decision 4 (per-entity pure updates writing only components of the same entity). Must ship with an explicit determinism argument at the loop per Decision 4, and must not introduce order-sensitive mutation, shared-state accumulation, RNG consumption, message emission, or entity creation/destruction in view-iteration order.

Note ADR-001 Decision 5: multi-component views spanning several migrated types are an explicitly scoped later optimisation, so keep this to a single-pool iteration unless the scope is widened deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: One hot CCmpPosition consumer iterates its storage pool directly instead of going through per-entity proxy accessors, with a determinism argument documented at the loop. Before/after numbers recorded showing the net effect of the CCmpPosition migration.

title: Guard the ResetState invariant: all proxies destroyed before the entt::registry object is replaced
description:
WHY: EnTTComponent<> (bd_0ad-1u1.1.3) caches an entt::registry* plus one storage-pool pointer per storage struct in each component proxy. Pool addresses are stable for the registry's lifetime (pools holds std::allocate_shared'd storage objects, so rehashing pools moves shared_ptrs, not the pooled objects), but they are NOT stable across replacement of the registry object itself. registry::swap() and operator=(basic_registry&&) (implemented as swap, registry.hpp:343) both invalidate every cached pool pointer, as does registry::reset(id) (registry.hpp:435), which erases a pool outright.

CComponentManager::ResetState() already satisfies the required invariant - the Deinit() + dealloc() loop runs before 'm_Registry = std::make_unique<entt::registry>()' - but this is currently only implied by statement ordering. Any future reordering silently produces proxies holding dangling pool pointers, which is a use-after-free with no diagnostic.

WHAT: add an ENSURE (or equivalent) in ResetState() asserting that no component proxies remain live at the point the registry is replaced (e.g. m_ComponentsByTypeId empty / a live-proxy counter at zero). Also consider a debug-only guard against registry::reset() ever being called. Deliberately NOT done in bd_0ad-1u1.1.3, whose acceptance criterion forbids CComponentManager call-site changes beyond the lifecycle hooks landed in bd_0ad-1u1.1.2. The invariant is documented in ADR-001 Appendix A.
acceptance_criteria: ResetState() fails loudly in a debug build if any component proxy is still live when the registry object is replaced. Existing test suite stays green.

title: Measure CCmpPosition port performance impact (before/after)
description:
WHY: the whole point of the EnTT migration is data layout and iteration cost. Milestone 1 is small enough that it may show no win, or even a small regression from the extra indirection through the registry - it is important to know which, before committing to migrating dozens more components on the assumption that it pays off. Google Benchmark and the benchmarks target are already wired up (libraries/source/benchmark, binaries/system/benchmarks.exe) and currently unused by simulation2.

WHAT:
- Add a benchmark exercising the realistic access patterns: per-entity ICmpPosition::GetPosition2D/MoveTo-style calls over a few thousand entities, plus the MT_TurnStart broadcast path, plus the MT_Interpolate path.
- Measure the pre-port and post-port builds and record numbers on this issue.
- Also capture a coarse whole-game signal (replay wall-clock time and/or Tracy capture of the simulation frame) since the microbenchmark may not reflect real cache behaviour.
- Report honestly: if the port is neutral or slightly slower at this stage, say so and note what would need to change (batch iteration replacing per-entity virtual calls) to realise the win.
acceptance_criteria: Before/after numbers for both the microbenchmark and a whole-replay run are recorded on this issue, with an explicit statement of whether milestone 1 is a perf win, neutral, or a regression, and why.

title: Document the component migration recipe and file follow-up ports
description:
WHY: milestone 1 only has lasting value if the next component takes hours instead of days. The knowledge gained during the CCmpPosition port needs to be captured as a repeatable recipe, and the remaining work needs to be visible in the tracker rather than living in one person's head.

WHAT:
- Write a short step-by-step migration recipe (audit state, define storage structs, port through the helper, verify serialization unchanged, run the determinism gate) next to the coexistence-layer code.
- Record the traps actually hit during the CCmpPosition port, especially anything about serialization order, entity lifetime, or interpolation state.
- Survey the remaining native (CT_Native, non-scripted) components and file bd issues for the next migration candidates, ordered by value and risk, as children of the epic bd_0ad-1u1.
- Explicitly note that CT_Script/CT_ScriptWrapper components remain out of scope and that a separate design effort is needed before they can be touched.
acceptance_criteria: A migration recipe exists in-repo; follow-up bd issues exist under epic bd_0ad-1u1 for the next candidate components; the scripted-component gap is filed as its own issue.

title: Unit tests for registry lifecycle, entity mapping, and component helper
description:
WHY: the coexistence layer is infrastructure that no gameplay code exercises yet, so it needs its own tests, or regressions will surface later as mysterious behaviour inside a ported component.

WHAT: extend/replace the placeholder source/simulation2/tests/test_EnTT.h (currently a bare registry smoke test) with real coverage:
- entity_id_t to entt::entity round-trips, including SYSTEM_ENTITY and local (ENTITY_TAGMASK) ids, and non-reuse of entity_id_t.
- Registry cleared correctly by ResetState; deferred destruction matching FlushDestroyedComponents semantics.
- A throwaway EnTT-backed test component driven through CComponentManager: Init, Serialize, Deserialize, Deinit, asserting serialized bytes are stable across runs and independent of entity creation order.
- Order-independence test: two sims reaching the same logical state via different creation/destruction orders produce identical ComputeStateHash output.

ACCEPTANCE: New tests pass in binaries/system/test.exe; the order-independence test genuinely fails if the helper is changed to serialize in storage order.
acceptance_criteria: New tests pass in binaries/system/test.exe; the order-independence test genuinely fails if the helper is changed to serialize in storage order.

title: Worker threads show as bare TIDs in Tracy
description: Tracy never receives thread names for worker threads because debug_SetThreadName (source/lib/sysdep/os/win/wdbg.cpp) early-returns unless a debugger is attached. Add a tracy::SetThreadName() call in source/ps/TaskManager.cpp (around where worker threads are spawned, ~line 253) so worker threads are labeled in the Tracy profiler instead of showing as bare TIDs.
design: Added tracy::SetThreadName(name.c_str()) call in WorkerThread::RunUntilDeath() (source/ps/TaskManager.cpp), right after the existing debug_SetThreadName() call and before g_Profiler2.RegisterCurrentThread(). Also added #include <tracy/Tracy.hpp>. This runs on the worker thread itself (called from within RunUntilDeath, the thread's own entry point), giving each worker a unique name like 'Task Mgr #N' visible in Tracy regardless of whether a debugger is attached. Verified source/ps/TaskManager.cpp compiles cleanly (isolated engine.vcxproj rebuild of TaskManager.obj succeeded with no errors); full solution build currently fails for unrelated pre-existing reasons (in-progress EnTT conversion work on this branch missing 'entt' in premake extern_libs for engine/gui/graphics projects) - not caused by or related to this change.
close_reason: Implemented and verified: tracy::SetThreadName() added to TaskManager.cpp worker thread entry point; TaskManager.cpp compiles cleanly in isolation.

title: FrameMark bisects the top-level PROFILE2 frame zone in Tracy timeline
description: FrameMark is called at the end of Frame()/NonVisualFrame() in main.cpp, but it falls inside the still-open PROFILE2("frame") zone entered earlier in the loop iteration. This means the frame boundary marker bisects the top-level zone in the Tracy timeline instead of aligning cleanly with it. Cosmetic trace-alignment issue; fixing it requires restructuring the scope of that top-level PROFILE2("frame") zone so it closes before FrameMark fires.
design: Wrapped the body of Frame() and NonVisualFrame() in source/main.cpp in a nested block scope containing the PROFILE2("frame") RAII guard (and the rest of the per-frame work), so the guard's destructor fires and closes the Tracy zone before the trailing FrameMark; call is reached. FrameMark; now sits just outside that block, after the zone has closed, instead of inside it. No frame logic/behavior changed; early-return paths (e.g. on shutdown) still skip FrameMark exactly as before, since the return still exits the enclosing function during stack unwind of the nested block.
close_reason: Restructured PROFILE2("frame") zone scope in source/main.cpp so it closes before FrameMark fires in both Frame() and NonVisualFrame(); cosmetic Tracy alignment fix, no behavior change.

title: Consider pointing entt include path at single_include amalgamated header for faster builds
description: WHY: discovered by perf-guru during review of bd_0ad-5je (entt Windows include path fix). The entt submodule ships a pre-amalgamated libraries/source/entt/entt/single_include/entt/entt.hpp in addition to the split libraries/source/entt/entt/src/entt tree that extern_libs5.lua now points at. Pointing the premake include path at single_include instead of src would cut preprocessor file-open churn across the ~10 projects that transitively pull in entt via ComponentManager.h. This is a build-time-only optimization with zero runtime/behavioral effect, but it does change which literal files get compiled, so it was deliberately kept out of bd_0ad-5je (which was scoped purely to fixing Windows include-path reproducibility, not changing which entt distribution form is used). Speculative/optional -- only worth doing if build times become a complaint.
acceptance_criteria: Either: (a) switch extern_libs5.lua's entt add_header_only_source_include_paths call to point at entt/single_include and confirm build times improve and all consumers still compile cleanly, or (b) close as won't-do if build-time impact is judged negligible.
